payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is her jacket fully closed?
node.criteria: Assess the same jacket's front closure using corresponding visible areas in SOURCE and EDITED, and inspect any directly visible closure cues in EDITED independently of cross-image correspondence. Score concrete visible movement of the front panels toward each other as partial fulfillment when an opening remains; score full fulfillment only when visible evidence shows the panels meeting along the closure with no visible opening remaining. Do not infer closure or progress from turning, swinging, draping, or occlusion. If the closure is not sufficiently visible in EDITED and no direct cue establishes its state, leave fulfillment unresolved.
node.binding: Compare the jacket on the woman in SOURCE with the jacket on the woman in EDITED. Judge the requested endpoint as a fully closed jacket, using corresponding visible portions where available and any directly visible closure cues in EDITED. Distinguish visible partial closure from no change; do not treat pose or obscuration as evidence of either. Use insufficient evidence when the closure state cannot be reliably determined.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: The closure is sufficiently visible to assess, and EDITED shows no concrete movement of the front panels toward closure relative to SOURCE, with no direct visible cue of closure progress.
node.half_when: Visible closure evidence shows concrete movement of the front panels toward each other relative to SOURCE, but a visible opening remains. If the closure is obscured and no direct cue establishes progress, leave the score unresolved rather than assigning partial fulfillment.
node.full_when: Visible evidence in EDITED shows the jacket’s front panels meeting along the closure, with no visible opening remaining along it; mere occlusion or draping does not establish this endpoint.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket’s front closure is visible in SOURCE, with the panels separated. In EDITED, the woman has turned and the jacket is swinging or draping; the closure is not clearly visible, and there is no direct cue that the panels moved toward each other or met. Pose and occlusion do not establish closure progress, so the requested change is not visibly demonstrated.
